subject: Acme long-context eval — next steps & model recommendations
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Acme long-context eval — next steps & model recommendations

Hi Sam — thanks again for a great discovery call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps based on what we heard from John and your team:

Call recap:
- Primary goal: reliably summarize and extract structured data from long legal/contract documents (typical doc sizes ~8k-20k tokens).
- Key constraints: high fidelity on summarization (no hallucinated clauses), deterministic truncation behavior, and enterprise-grade audit logs.
- Throughput/latency target: sub-1s per 512-token chunk for interactive review, batch overnight runs for large corpora.

Initial model fit thoughts:
- Recommendation 1 (best quality, long-context): redwood/falcon-90b-ctx32k-quant — good baseline for 32k windows, best on extractive fidelity but higher cost.
- Recommendation 2 (cost/latency balance): open-llama-30b-ctx64k — larger context but varies on summarization fidelity; we recommend fine-tuning prompt sets.
- Recommendation 3 (low-cost multi-pass): small encoder + long-context retriever pipeline (embedding + chunking + summarizer) for very long docs (>64k).

Attachments I will send after this note: prompt_sets_v1.txt (sample prompt templates we used in the call) and acme_long_context_eval_results.csv (initial eval run on your redacted corpus). Also sharing the benchmark dashboard link in case you want to review metrics live.

Primary concerns we flagged on the call:
- Truncation behavior: different models drop context differently (head vs tail). We should run targeted tests to confirm which truncation strategy matches your worst-case docs.
- Summarization fidelity: for legal clauses we saw a small number of paraphrase/omission errors in the baseline — we'll provide prompt adjustments and a small eval suite to track regressions.

Proposed next steps / mutual action plan:
1) Acme: share a redacted sample set (5-10 representative docs, S3 or Drive link).
2) Redwood: run a 10k-doc simulated pass (10 representative long docs across sizes) on Dedicated capacity and return a short report by 7/22.
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with Dev (cc'd) on 7/22 to validate integration paths and infra requirements.
4) Commercials: I'll loop in our pricing note once we have the exact throughput target (we can do a provisional estimate now).

If that plan looks good, can you confirm Sam and cc John for procurement? Happy to book the 30-min deep-dive — propose 7/22 10:00am PT.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Acme long-context eval — artifacts & model bench summary

Hi Sam / John — attaching the initial artifacts from our sandbox run. Summary highlights below and a short technical appendix attached.

What we ran:
- 10 representative long documents (8k-22k tokens) using your redacted corpus.
- Evaluations: ROUGE / exact-clause-match, hallucination checks (clause omission), and context-preservation tests (head/tail retention).

Key results (see acme_long_context_eval_results.csv):
- redwood/falcon-90b-ctx32k-quant: highest clause-match (92%) but avg token cost ~3.8x open-llama-30b. Truncation: drops oldest context first in our infra (configurable).
- open-llama-30b-ctx64k: good window size, clause-match 86%, lower cost/latency tradeoff. Some summarization condensation that needs prompt adjustments.
- Retriever + summarizer pipeline: best cost profile for >64k docs, but increases end-to-end latency and requires embedding index maintenance.

Recommended short-term plan:
1) Run a 10k-doc batch on Dedicated (we can provision a small pool) to validate cost projections and measure tail-case behavior. (Action: Redwood)
2) Build a 50-item prompt/eval set focused on 'critical clause fidelity' and run nightly regression checks for 2 weeks. (Action: Redwood + Acme)
3) For interactive review UI, start with redwood/falcon-90b-ctx32k-quant canary and fall back to retriever pipeline for extremely long docs.

Links and artifacts: prompt_sets_v1.txt attached; dashboard link provided for per-run metrics. Also POC notes about truncation strategies (head-truncate vs tail-truncate) are in the Drive doc.

Next steps:
- Sam: confirm access method for sample corpus (S3 share or Drive) and procurement timeline.
- John: if procurement wants an estimated TCO we can provide a 2-line pricing estimate by EOD today pending throughput numbers.

Thanks — happy to walk through any of the rows in the CSV on the tech call.

Best,
Marissa

Nice work Marissa — quick internal note before the 7/22 deep-dive.

Technical notes / risks:
- We should be explicit with Acme about the quantization/regression risk. Large-quantized 90b models can show subtle fidelity regressions; recommend a small fine-tune or prompt-tuning pass on their redacted set before rolling to production.
- For truncation testing, we should include both head- and tail-masking strategies and capture exact-token offsets where content is lost; add those columns to the CSV.
- Dev, please provision a short-lived Dedicated pool (3 gpus) for the 10k-doc run and output per-doc latency histograms + token-cost estimates. Include kernel/compilation flags and quant profile used.

I'll draft a one-pager for procurement on cost/latency options once we have the per-token numbers.

Rishi
VP, Applied ML & Inference
Redwood Inference
